text_blocks.snippet: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) has a high recurrence rate, often within one to two years of initial diagnosis due to its aggressive nature and tendency to be diagnosed at later stages. Recurrence can manifest with various symptoms depending on the location of the recurrence, including pain, fatigue, skin changes, and even neurological issues if it spreads to the brain. Treatment for recurrent SCLC is typically palliative and may involve chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or other approaches, with the goal of managing symptoms and improving quality of life.
